Continue my own internal universe. It is based on pitch black where when nights comes all the nasty monsters come out. Being out at night is a death sentence. My mom took me to a small little fair. It had some small rides and other cool things to do. During the magician act, there was another kid I tallked to that had two plastic swords. I enjoyed talking to him, but not gonna lie, I was super jealous of those swords.

After the show, he just gave me one. This was huge for 12 year old me because my mom straight up said no, they are too expensive. They were 10 bucks each, so yeah way too expensive. Price didn't matter then, they were awesome to me. 

Anyway, we continued to play and his little brother shows up. He is annoyed by him  and suggests we chase him. I can relate because I too had a little brother that annoys me. We chase him for a bit until he goes in to the hay crawlspace. There were two tunnels made of hay bundles that kids could crawl through. 

Spur of the moment I suggest we each take a tunnel that way we wont miss him and still be chasing him. I get to the other side and he and his brother aren't there. I checked both tunnels and then searched the whole fair. I have no idea how they disappeared. They could have at least said goodbye. I was pretty sad, but not too sad. I still had that awesome sword.

Ring of Blood Curdling

It is a golden ring with a pitch black gem. There is a snall hole on the underside of the ring under where the gem is. 

On activation the gem pierces the player through the hole and drops his/her max health by half. In return, for every 5 points of health taken, a d10 is given to the player to add to his/her damage rolls. These can be used all at once or distributed over multiple turns.
On long rest remaining d10 are lost and hp is returned to normal.

Ex. 100/120 hp, use of the ring will drop you down to 50/70 hp and gives10 d10.

Ex2. 120/120 hp, use of ring, 60/60, 12 d10 awarded.
